measurement.rest_rule: Resting voltage is read at least 90 minutes after a charge or flight.
measurement.ir_rule: IR is measured solo only (one pack on a channel); IR read on a parallel board is not used.
from_logs: solo cell IR on every storage run (performance notes and the 2x single-cell check)
first-line cell voltages (deep-discharge pull check, and advisories for the board checks)
storage-end voltages, for the self-discharge check when a pack did not fly in between
not_from_logs: pack temperature: the DX8 logs show only the charger's own temperature, so heat is reported by hand
swelling, pouch damage, connector damage and abnormal charging behaviour: reported by hand
flight times: the first log line may be less than 90 minutes after a flight, so voltage checks from logs are advisories
the board checks themselves (0.60 V pack spread, 0.10 V per cell, 0.10 V in-pack, 2.0 to 3.0 V cells): read at the board before connecting

steps: Select the flown series and include every active pack in them. Empty and pulled slots are skipped: a pulled pack gets no storage charge, and nothing is reordered.
Order each channel by series, then by pack number.
On each charger, run Channel 1 and Channel 2 in rounds: start Channel 1, then Channel 2, and wait for both before the next round. When one channel is empty, the other continues alone.
Count the files per charger: one log file per pack.

start_order.rule: On each charger, start Channel 1, then Channel 2, then wait for both to finish before the next round. When one channel runs out, the other carries on.
start_order.mapping: Logs map by charger, channel and order (one log file per pack).

conditions: Before connecting, read each pack's resting voltage at least 90 minutes after its last charge or flight.

Charge a pack alone that night (it stays in rotation, no status change) if: the board's packs are more than 0.60 V apart; any cell is more than 0.10 V from the same-position cell of another pack on the board; its own cells are more than 0.10 V apart; a cell rests between 2.0 and 3.0 V; or a connector is damaged (fix it first).

Board warning: if a port fuse blows or a balance-pin light comes on, stop the charge, find the outlier pack and charge it alone. If the same pack keeps causing it, its own gap to the board tightens to 0.30 V.

Per-cell check: on 2026-10-11 the first log readings had same-position cells more than 0.10 V apart (C1-P5, C1-P6). Those readings may be less than 90 minutes after a flight, so check resting voltage before connecting.

self_discharge_checks.pull_rule: P5 (pull): after a balanced storage charge, one cell drops 0.05 V or more more than the other cells within 48 to 72 hours, or any cell loses about 0.10 V within 24 hours.
self_discharge_checks.how_we_check: compare the first line of the next storage log with the end of the last storage run, for a pack that did not fly in between (the upload note lists the flown series or packs).
self_discharge_checks.longer_gaps: if more than 72 hours passed, a relative drop under 0.05 V clears the check; 0.05 V or more is not proof, so it is an advisory to recheck within 48 to 72 hours.
self_discharge_checks.performance_grade: scaled to 7 days: 10 mV or less pass, 10 to 30 mV borderline, over 30 mV fail. The grade is a note only, never a reason to retire a pack.

notes: Charge every series that was flown, all of it, including any packs in it that did not fly. Series that were not flown stay off.
Each pack has a permanent home channel; empty and pulled slots are skipped and nothing is reordered.
C1-P1 is back from the D pool from the next storage night (same pack, same history); it charges on DX8-1 Channel 1.
Add the flown series or packs and the days since last use to the upload note.

Pull a pack only for fire risk: swelling or pouch damage, charge heat of 45 °C or more or clearly hotter than its siblings, a cell under 1.5 V (or under 2.0 V for about a week), self-discharge, or abnormal behaviour on a solo charge. A pulled pack is not charged.

Charge a pack alone that night (it stays in rotation) for the board checks: 0.60 V pack spread, a cell 0.10 V from its same-position cell on another pack, 0.10 V spread inside the pack, a cell resting 2.0 to 3.0 V, a damaged connector, or a cell IR step of 2x its own level and the pack median.
Board warning (HGLRC Thor 6-port): a blown port fuse or a lit balance-pin light means the outlier pack charges alone; a pack that keeps causing it gets a 0.30 V gap of its own.
Storage nights apply only the pull list.
IR trend, board IR match and single-cell IR are performance notes only.
